title: OMC-1 dust polarization in ALMA Band 7: diagnosing grain alignment mechanisms in the vicinity of Orion Source I
question: Whether a single model, or a single grain alignment mechanism, is sufficient to explain the complex polarisation morphology observed in the vicinity of Orion Source I in OMC-1.

data.angular_resolution: 0.54'' x 0.43'', oriented -74 deg E of N
data.sensitivity: 0.62 mJy/beam (mosaicked Stokes Q and U RMS)

what.value: Large-scale magnetic field orientation in OMC-1 (-64.2 +/- 6.5 deg E of N, i.e., 116 deg E of N)

evidence.quote: The clump which we observe, in the centre of the OMC-1 region, has an approximately linear magnetic field across it ((cite: chrysostomou1994), (cite: simpson2006), (cite: pattle2017)), with an orientation $-64^{\circ}.2\pm6^{\circ}.5$ E of N (cite: wardthompson2017).

Throughout the following discussion we principally compare the polarisation geometry in each region to three models: polarisation arising from grains aligned (1) with their major axes perpendicular to the large-scale 116$^{\circ}$ E of N magnetic field (polarisation angle $26^{\circ}$ E of N) observed on larger scales in the region

what.value: Magnetic field strength B = 9.4 +/- 1.8 mG, density n_H2 = 2.7 x 10^8 cm^-3, and magnetic Reynolds number R_m = 1.7 x 10^5 in OMC-1

evidence.quote: (cite: cortes2020) find $B = 9.4 \pm 1.8$ mG at $n_{\textsc{h}_{2}} = 2.7\times 10^{8}$ cm$^{-3}$.

evidence.loc: Discussion of grain alignment in the Anomalous Region/Fork
evidence.quote: (cite: cortes2020) find a magnetic Reynolds number $R_{m} = 1.7\times 10^{5}\gg 1$ in OMC-1, indicating that the magnetic field is well-coupled to the gas.

what.value: Source I minor axis orientation (53 deg) and disc physical size (~100 au)

evidence.quote: The disc itself, with physical size $\sim 100$ au (cite: ginsburg2018) and a major axis of 0.23$^{\prime\prime}$ at 340 GHz (cite: wright2020) is smaller than the beam.

inconsistent with the polarisation having arisen from a $116^{\circ}\pm 6.5^{\circ}$ magnetic field, but consistent with being parallel to the minor axis of Source I ($53^{\circ}$; (cite: ginsburg2018)).

what.value: Source I disc spectral index (~2 to ~3) and inclination limits (79 +/- 1 deg and 74 +/- 1 deg)

evidence.quote: (cite: wright2020) find a spectral index $\sim$2 along the disc mid-plane consistent with optically thick dust emission.

(cite: wright2020), observing at 340 GHz, set a lower limit to the disc inclination of $79^{\circ}\pm1^{\circ}$ (with major and minor axes $99\times19$ au) at a disc brightness temperature contour of 400 K, and $74^{\circ}\pm1^{\circ}$ ($239\times45$ au) at a disc brightness temperature contour of 25K

what.value: Position and properties of the HCN / H3CN ring feature near SMA 1

evidence.quote: (cite: wright2017) identified a ring of emission near SMA 1 in HCN 354.5 GHz and H$_{3}$CN 354.7 GHz emission, which they interpreted as evidence for passage of debris from the BN/KL explosion.

what.value: Luminosity (> 10^4 L_sun) and effective brightness temperature (~ 1500 K) of Source I

evidence.quote: The luminosity of Source I is not well-characterised, but is thought to be $> 10^{4}$ L$_{\odot}$ (cite: menten1995).
The effective brightness temperature of Source I is $\sim 1500$ K (cite: reid2007), and so from Wien’s Law, we infer a peak emission wavelength of photons emanating from Source I of $\sim 1.9\,\mu$m.

what.value: Peak H2 column densities in the Fork (MF2: 3.1 x 10^24 cm^-2) and Main Ridge (5.4 x 10^24 cm^-2)

evidence.loc: Discussion of grain alignment in the Anomalous Region/Fork
evidence.quote: The peak column density in emission potentially associated with the Fork is $N_{\textsc{h}_{2}} = 3.1\times 10^{24}\,$cm$^{-2}$, as measured at the methyl formate peak MF2 (cite: favre2011).

evidence.loc: B-RAT versus k-RAT alignment in the Ridge
evidence.quote: The material of the Ridge has a higher column density ($N_{\textsc{h}_{2}} = 5.4\times 10^{24}$ cm$^{-2}$; (cite: favre2011)) than its surroundings, corresponding to a peak $K$-band extinction $A_{K}\sim 500$.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, mosaic, and regrid Stokes I, Q, and U maps
recipe.method: Calibrate and image individual fields in CASA using spw0-2, linearly mosaic the three pointings using Miriad linmos with primary beam weighting and taper option, and regrid onto a 0.25'' pixel grid.
key_parameters: Briggs weighting with robust = 0.5, cell size = 0.060'', regridded to 0.25'' pixel grid
assumptions: Spectral lines in spw0-2 contribute negligible polarised signal

recipe.goal: Calculate polarised intensity, polarisation angles, and sub-region statistics
recipe.method: Compute polarised intensity PI = sqrt(Q^2 + U^2) (without debiasing at high SNR), apply a 6 mJy/beam threshold, compute polarisation angles theta = 0.5 arctan(U/Q) and uncertainties delta_theta = 0.5 * delta_Q / PI, and calculate mean and median angles in 5 defined sub-regions.
key_parameters: PI threshold >= 6 mJy/beam; delta_Q = delta_U = 0.62 mJy/beam; delta_theta <= 3.0 deg
assumptions: RMS uncertainties on Stokes Q and U emission are equal

recipe.goal: Compare observed polarisation geometries in sub-regions against geometric models using Monte Carlo KS and Kuiper tests
recipe.method: Predict pixel-by-pixel polarisation angles for geometric models (uniform 26 deg E of N, concentric around BN/KL, concentric around Source I, concentric around ring feature), perturb model angles with Gaussian noise of width sigma_theta (1 to 20 deg) 1000 times per sigma_theta, and run two-sided KS and Kuiper tests against observed angle distributions.
key_parameters: sigma_theta in range 1 deg - 20 deg; 1000 Monte Carlo realisations per sigma_theta; consistency criterion p > 0.05
assumptions: Large-scale magnetic field has orientation 116 deg E of N (polarisation angle 26 deg E of N); additional angular dispersion arises from Alfvenic distortion by non-thermal gas motions

recipe.goal: Estimate characteristic grain alignment and damping timescales in the Anomalous Region/Fork
recipe.method: Analytically evaluate and compare the Larmor precession timescale (tau_Lar), mechanical alignment timescale (tau_mech), radiative precession timescale (tau_rad,p), and gas damping timescale (tau_gas) as functions of grain size a.
assumptions: Paramagnetic grains with rho = 3 g cm^-3, axial ratio s = 0.5; unobscured radiation from Source I with anisotropy gamma ~ 1 and RAT efficiency |Q_Gamma| <= 0.4; thermal grain rotation (omega ~ omega_th); subsonic drift (Delta v < c_s) for v-MATs.

answer_key.quantity: Inferred dust grain size in Source I disc for self-scattering at 870 um

evidence.quote: At 870$\mu$m, this implies the existence of a population of dust grains with sizes $\sim 140\,\mu$m or larger in the Source I disc.

If scattering is significant at 345 GHz but negligible at 96 GHz, this puts strong constraints on the grain size distribution in the Source I disc, with a significant population of grains with sizes $\sim 140\,\mu$m, but a cut-off in grain size at $<\,500\,\mu$m.

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit angular dispersion sigma_theta (Eastern arm of Fork, Main Ridge, MF4/MF5)

evidence.quote: The best agreement between the BN/KL-concentric model and our data occurs for $\sigma_{\theta} = 8^{\circ}$, but $p > 0.05$ agreement occurs up to $\sigma_{\theta} \approx 13^{\circ}$ (KS test), or in the range $4.5^{\circ}\lesssim \sigma_{\theta}\lesssim 12.5^{\circ}$ (Kuiper test).
The best agreement with the data is at $\sigma_{\theta} = 8^{\circ}$, matching the equivalent value in the eastern arm of the Fork.

A wide range of angular dispersion values, $\sigma_{\theta} \gtrsim 4.5^{\circ}$ (KS test) or $2.5^{\circ} \lesssim \sigma_{\theta} \lesssim 17.5^{\circ}$ (Kuiper test), produce patterns consistent with the small sample of observed vectors, but the best agreement is found at $\sigma_{\theta} \sim 8^{\circ}$, matching the equivalent values in the eastern arm of the Fork and the Ridge.

answer_key.quantity: Consistent angular dispersion sigma_theta in Western arm of Fork

evidence.quote: In the western arm, $p > 0.05$ agreement between the Source-I-concentric model and our data occurs at $\sigma_{\theta} < 8^{\circ}$ (KS test), or $\sigma_{\theta} < 5^{\circ}$ (Kuiper test).

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that Source I’s extreme luminosity may be sufficient to make the radiative precession timescale shorter than the Larmor timescale for moderately large grains ($> 0.005-0.1\,\mu$m), causing them to precess around the radiation anisotropy vector (k-RATs) rather than the magnetic field direction (B-RATs).
